svg.text: Browser agents: a real CVE, and the mitigation that actually works
"The Hidden Dangers of Browsing AI Agents" — Mudryi, Chaklosh, Wójcik (ARIMLABS.AI), arXiv 2505.13076
CVE-2025-47241 (CVSS 9.3, Critical) — a domain allowlist that trusts its own URL parsing
Browser Use's allowlist check split a URL on ":" and compared the result against an operator-configured allowlist — it never accounted for HTTP Basic Auth syntax.
https://example.com:pass@localhost:8080
"example.com" is a USERNAME here, not the hostname
Agent believes: "example.com" (allowed) ✓
Real destination: localhost:8080 (never allowed)
The agent's own belief about its boundary was wrong — and it had no way to know. A textbook SSRF enabler, combined with the prompt-injection bug
below, a path to full agent hijacking. Fixed upstream in v0.1.45. This is application-level trust in the agent's own URL parsing — exactly the
class of check that a network-layer, default-deny egress firewall makes irrelevant regardless of any parsing bug inside the container.
Mitigation effectiveness, as reported in the paper's own benchmarks

g.text: 0% attack success — the only mitigation that reaches this

svg.text: Why planner/executor isolation wins — and the direct line to JiMesh
A PLANNER component only ever sees trusted, pre-vetted input and makes decisions. A separate EXECUTOR component is the only one that touches
untrusted content (the raw page HTML) and holds actual tool/browser privilege. A security monitor enforces that untrusted data can never flow
back into the planner's own reasoning — the decision-maker never sees what the attacker controls.
This is architecturally the same shape as JiMesh's own tool-call flow: the OPA capability decision happens BEFORE the subagent's container
executes anything, evaluated against server-side policy the agent's own output cannot influence — the planner/executor split, just for tool calls
instead of a DOM.
The field is still building this out — but the best-known answer is an architecture choice, not a bolt-on filter, and JiMesh already has that shape.
